# Bullets from the players ship should always fall on the beat

## Problem statement

Player auto-fire currently uses per-weapon cooldowns started at collection time (`src/utils/weapons.ts`, `Player.tryFire`), so shots drift relative to any musical pulse and different active weapons fire out of phase. Make every player shot land on a shared musical grid: player fire is globally quantised to an **80 BPM** beat, and every weapon's fire rate is an exact subdivision of that beat. The values are configurable rather than hard-coded.

## Users

- **Player** — wants the ship's shots to feel rhythmically locked to a consistent 80 BPM pulse, so the auto-fire has a musical cadence even with no background music.
- **AI agents / developers** — need a single, pure beat-clock module and a catalogue-wide invariant so any current or future weapon (e.g. the planned 20 BPM quarter-time large/explosive bullet) can be added without accidentally firing off the beat.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want my ship's bullets to leave on the beat, so the auto-fire feels deliberate and rhythmic rather than mechanically drifting.
- As a **player**, I want every weapon I collect to keep firing in time with the same beat, so switching weapons never makes the rhythm stumble.
- As a **developer**, I want a weapon's fire rate to be expressed as a subdivision of the beat and validated by a test, so I cannot add an off-grid weapon by mistake.
- As a **developer**, I want the BPM and per-weapon subdivisions to be configurable, so the feel can be tuned (and tested) without editing hard-coded literals.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Pure, configurable 80 BPM beat clock.** A new pure, unit-testable module (e.g. `src/utils/beat.ts`) derives the beat period from a **configurable** BPM (default **80 BPM** → 750 ms/beat), tracks a beat anchor/time origin, and exposes a quantisation helper that maps an arbitrary elapsed time to the next beat/subdivision tick (`nextTick(t)`, `isOnBeat/fireTimeFor(interval, t)`, etc.). No `Date`/frame coupling; deterministic given an input time.
- [ ] **AC2 — All player fire is globally quantised.** Player auto-fire (`Player.tryFire` and its callers in `CombatScene`/`GymWeapons`) emits shots only on ticks of the shared beat clock, phase-locked to the scene/beat anchor — never off-grid — regardless of when a weapon is collected or the frame rate. All simultaneously active weapons fire on the same shared grid (no independent, drifting cooldowns). Tests assert every emitted shot time is an exact grid tick.
- [ ] **AC3 — Per-weapon subdivisions + catalogue-wide invariant.** Each weapon's fire interval is an exact subdivision of the beat: **cannon 375 ms (160 BPM, 2/beat)**, **spread 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat)**, **dual 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat)**, **rapid 125 ms (480 BPM, 6/beat)**. A catalogue-wide test asserts every `WeaponDefinition.fireRateMs` satisfies `beatPeriodMs % fireRateMs === 0` (equivalently `fireRateMs × n === beatPeriodMs` for a positive integer `n`), so the future 20 BPM quarter-time weapon and any other new weapon are on-grid by construction.
- [ ] **AC4 — All values configurable.** BPM, the per-weapon subdivisions/fire rates, and the quantisation behaviour are configurable through the project's existing config plumbing (`src/core/rules.ts` and/or `src/core/config.ts`/`constants.ts`; persisted where the existing pattern persists), with sane defaults — no scattered hard-coded beat/rate literals. Tests assert a config override changes the firing cadence.
- [ ] **AC5 — Testing/validation.** Unit tests cover the beat module (period from BPM, quantisation boundaries/edge cases, config override), the catalogue invariant (AC3), and `Player.tryFire`/auto-fire emitting only on grid ticks with multiple active weapons phase-locked. Scene-level tests (gameHarness) assert real bullet spawns land on grid ticks across multiple frames and are framerate-independent. All tests serve a distinct behaviour.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries — in particular GDD §2.3/§4.4 (the "Cannon fires every ~400 ms" wording and the weapon fire-rate description) and any beat/config tuning docs.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine/stack:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript, Vite, Vitest (locked). No external art/audio assets.
- **Silent timing grid only:** per producer, the beat is an internal scheduling contract — **no audible metronome and no background music** (GDD §7.3/§8 keep music out of MVP scope). No beat audio/visual indicator is in scope.
- **Player bullets only:** enemy fire timing is unchanged (the item is titled "from the players ship").
- **Scope:** applies to all scenes that auto-fire the player (PlayScene via `CombatScene`, and the gym scenes reusing `Player`), through one shared beat module — not per-scene duplicates.
- **Beat anchor:** the beat clock is anchored at scene/player start and advances with game time (pauses with the game if paused).
- **No behaviour change beyond timing:** weapon patterns, bullet visuals, lifetimes, cumulative+timed semantics and Reset behaviour are unchanged; only fire timing changes.

## Existing state

- `src/utils/weapons.ts` defines `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` with hard-coded `fireRateMs` (cannon 400, spread 600, dual 500, rapid 125) and `bulletLifetime` values; heading/pattern math is pure.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` holds per-weapon cooldowns in `_weaponCooldowns` and `tryFire(dt)` re-arms a fired weapon's cooldown to its own `fireRateMs` (independent timers, phase set by collection time). Cumulative + timed semantics (`equipWeapon`, `resetWeapon`, `tickWeaponTimers`) are implemented and tested.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` (`_autoFire`) and `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` (`_autoFire`) call `player.tryFire(dt)` each frame and spawn bullets via `createBulletsFromHeading`/`angleToVelocity`.
- **No beat/BPM/clock infrastructure exists anywhere in `src/`**; there is no music system (GDD §7.3 out-of-MVP).
- Config precedent: `src/core/rules.ts` (localStorage-persisted `GameRules`, e.g. power-up spawn interval) and `src/core/config.ts`/`configTypes.ts` (CSV-backed ship config). `src/core/constants.ts` holds `WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS` etc.
- Related completed work: AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR (weapon catalogue + auto-fire), AH-0MUD9R3070063DDR (`tryFire` extraction), AH-0MTV7RITM009LJF6 (cumulative/timed weapons), AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0 (bullet lifetimes).

## Desired change

1. Add a pure **beat module** (`src/utils/beat.ts`): BPM → beat period, beat anchor, and quantisation helpers (`nextSubdivisionTick`, `shotTimeFor`, `isOnGrid`). Configurable BPM (default 80).
2. Re-express each `WeaponDefinition` fire rate as a **beat subdivision** (cannon 2/beat, spread 1/beat, dual 1/beat, rapid 6/beat) derived from the beat period; add the catalogue-wide on-grid invariant test.
3. Replace per-weapon free-running cooldowns in `Player.tryFire` with **phase-locked scheduling**: a weapon's next shot time is the smallest multiple of its interval at/after the current beat-clock time (anchored at the shared beat origin), so every shot lands on a grid tick and active weapons stay in phase. Collection may delay the first shot to the next grid tick (by design).
4. Wire the shared beat clock into `CombatScene._autoFire` and `GymWeapons._autoFire` (and any other `Player.tryFire` callers) so the scene supplies/uses the same clock.
5. Make BPM and the per-weapon subdivisions **configurable** through the existing config plumbing with defaults, rather than literals.
6. Update unit + scene-harness tests (existing `weapons.test.ts`, `Player.test.ts`, `GymWeapons.test.ts`, `CombatScene` tests) and documentation (GDD §2.3/§4.4, README).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/utils/beat.ts` — **NEW** — pure, configurable 80 BPM beat clock + quantisation helpers.
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — fire rates re-expressed as beat subdivisions; catalogue-wide on-grid invariant.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `tryFire`/cooldown model → phase-locked scheduling on the shared beat clock.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `_autoFire` drives the shared beat clock.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — `_autoFire` drives the shared beat clock.
- `src/core/rules.ts` / `src/core/config.ts` (and/or `src/core/constants.ts`) — configurable BPM + per-weapon subdivisions with defaults.
- `src/utils/weapons.test.ts`, **NEW** `src/utils/beat.test.ts`, `src/entities/Player.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.test.ts` — coverage for quantisation, invariant and scene emission.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §2.3/§4.4; `README.md` — document the beat-aligned fire model.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Gameplay-feel change:** current rates (cannon 400 → 375 ms; spread 600 → 750 ms; dual 500 → 750 ms; rapid 125 unchanged) slightly change DPS/cadence, and collection now delays the first shot to the next grid tick. Assumption: acceptable and intended ("must always fall on the beat").
- **Definition of "the beat" without music:** resolved by the producer — silent internal grid; no audible/visual reference. The beat is only observable through bullet cadence and tests.
- **Config surface choice:** the producer requires configurability, but the exact home (localStorage rules vs CSV ship config vs constants) is a planning decision; the ACs require at least one tested override path.
- **Phase-locking and multiple weapons:** cumulative weapons with different subdivisions must share the anchor; an implementation that keeps independent cooldowns will drift — the AC2 test guards this.
- **Frame quantisation edge cases:** shots must be attributed to the correct grid tick under variable `dt` (including large deltas), and remain framerate-independent — explicit boundary tests required.
- **Scope-creep risk:** audible beat/music, enemy fire quantisation, and beat-synced visuals are out of scope; record as linked work items rather than folding in.

## Related work

- **AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR** (completed) — "Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene": origin of `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`, the fire-rate constants and `Player` auto-fire this item re-times.
- **AH-0MUD9R3070063DDR** (completed) — "Extract auto-fire with onWeaponFired hook": the `tryFire` auto-fire architecture being changed.
- **AH-0MTV7RITM009LJF6** (completed) — "Make weapons both cumalative and time out": cumulative per-weapon timers/cooldowns.
- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** (completed) — "Bullets should have a distance and should wrap around the screen": per-weapon bullet lifetimes adjacent to the fire-rate config.
- **AH-0MTGS8TWU006WTFX** (completed) — "Wire shoot audio into GymWeapons._autoFire()": fire cues whose cadence follows the fire rate.
- **AH-0MT7UW0Y80062NU1** (completed) — "Bring simple audio effects into MVP scope in GDD": the audio-scope boundary (no music).
- **GDD (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5)** — §2.3 auto-fire (~400 ms wording), §4.4 weapon fire rates/lifetimes, §7.3 audio (music out of scope), §8 future scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Beat semantics — (a) per-weapon beat-subdivision intervals with independent cooldowns, or (b) a single 80 BPM clock with every shot snapped to the next grid tick?" — Answer (producer, interactive): **(b) global beat quantisation**. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "What is the beat reference — (a) silent internal grid only, (b) audible metronome, or (c) visual beat indicator?" — Answer (producer, interactive): **(a) silent internal grid only** (no music; consistent with GDD §7.3). Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Per-weapon subdivisions and the catalogue-wide invariant?" — Answer (producer, interactive): **as recommended** — cannon 375 ms (160 BPM, 2/beat), spread 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat), dual 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat), rapid 125 ms (480 BPM, 6/beat); invariant `beatPeriodMs % fireRateMs === 0` enforced for the whole catalogue. Source: interactive reply.
- Producer note (interactive, given alongside the answers to Q1–Q3): **all values must be configurable** (BPM, per-weapon subdivisions, quantisation behaviour). Source: interactive reply.

> Prior answers changed: none — all answers above are the final accepted versions.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** – Bullets should have a distance and should wrap around the screen (completed)
- **AH-0MUFGUR9C003XD77** – GitHub Pages deploy rejects release tags (environment policy allows only dev) (in-progress)
- **AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ** – Gym index scene (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: add, always, assert, based, beat (+30 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: add, always, based, beat, bullet (+29 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: add, always, assert, based, belongs (+28 more)

## Plan (plan_complete)

Decomposed into 8 child work items (test-first / vertical-slice), all at
stage `intake_complete`:

**Phase 1 — Foundation**

**Phase 2 — Grid + invariant**

- Make BPM and per-weapon subdivisions configurable via existing config plumbing (AH-0MUGY84L1004H2UP)

**Phase 3 — Emission + wiring**
- Replace Player.tryFire per-weapon cooldowns with phase-locked beat scheduling (AH-0MUGQCMNA0061J4A)
- Wire the shared beat clock into CombatScene and GymWeapons auto-fire (AH-0MUGY7ZUO008QSUX)

**Phase 4 — Verification + handoff**

**Dependency edges:** T2→T1, T3→T1, T4→T3, T5→{T1,T2}, T6→T4,

# Problem statement

The audit runner's parent-first flow re-audits all children on every run because the freshness fingerprint includes the global git HEAD sha. In `--child-in-main-slot` mode, non-interactive runs leave all children with `partial` verdicts, which blocks the parent from recording a "Ready to close: Yes" result even when all parent ACs are met. This prevents audit completion for epics whose children were previously audited.

# Users

- **Audit runner / downtime worker** — expects a non-interactive audit of an epic to produce a valid verdict without requiring a live agent session.
- **Producer / human reviewer** — expects the audit to accurately reflect whether work is ready to close, not to block on stale or unserviced child verdicts.

# Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Fingerprint scoping.** `_compute_content_fingerprint` no longer includes the global git HEAD sha as a sole invalidation trigger; instead it is scoped to child-relevant key files and/or commits so that unrelated HEAD movement on `dev` does not invalidate previously valid child audits.
- **AC2 — In-main-slot partial verdict handling.** When a child's `ac_results` remain `partial` because the invoking agent session never serviced the `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items, the parent audit treats those verdicts as "not assessed" (inherits the child's previously stored verdict or marks them reusable) rather than blocking the parent's readiness-to-close decision.
- **AC3 — Diagnostic clarity.** The audit output surfaces a clear, machine-parseable diagnostic that distinguishes a "child partial because unserviced in-main-slot" verdict from a genuine "not-ready" child verdict, including the reason code in the audit summary.
- **AC4 — No regression on interactive runs.** The above fixes do not change the behaviour of interactive audit runs (where an agent session *can* service in-main-slot items); those continue to honour the full in-main-slot workflow.
- **AC5 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** Run the complete suite and confirm zero failures.

# Constraints

- The fix must not introduce a new mode flag or require operator configuration; it should be the default behaviour.
- The fix should be backward-compatible with persisted audit results (old fingerprint format should still be readable).
- The change scope is the audit runner's child freshness logic (`_compute_content_fingerprint`, `_child_content_changed`), the in-main-slot verdict accumulation logic (`_build_issue_json`, `all_ac_acceptable`), and the diagnostic output path.

# Existing state

- `_compute_content_fingerprint` includes the current git HEAD sha — any new commit on `dev` invalidates every stored child audit.
- In `child_in_main_slot=True` mode, child Phase-1 AC screens and Phase-2 deep analysis emit `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items for the invoking session. In non-interactive runs, these are never serviced and stay `partial`.
- `_build_issue_json` includes child AC verdicts in `all_ac_acceptable`, so the parent is reported "Ready to close: No" even when all parent ACs are met.
- The runner's terminal lifecycle then demotes parent and children to `open`/`plan_complete` as a side effect.

# Desired change

1. **Scope the fingerprint**: Replace the global HEAD sha in `_compute_content_fingerprint` with a child-scoped hash (key files + relevant commits).
2. **Handle partial verdicts**: When computing `all_ac_acceptable`, skip children whose verdict is `partial` due to unserviced in-main-slot items — treat them as "not assessed" rather than "not accepted."
3. **Add diagnostics**: In the audit summary, emit a reason code or flag indicating when a child's `partial` verdict is due to unserviced in-main-slot items vs. genuine assessment failure.

# Key Files (predicted)

- `src/audit/` or equivalent audit runner module — `_compute_content_fingerprint`, `_child_content_changed`, `_build_issue_json`, in-main-slot verdict handling
- `scripts/audit_runner*` or equivalent — runner invocation, non-interactive path
- Audit output/summary formatter — diagnostic message generation

# Related work

- **AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO** — Unify PlayScene/GymFormationScene combat logic (completed): the parent epic that discovered this issue during audit.
- **SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F** — Audit parent-first flow (internal assertion): the flow that triggers the re-audit on stale children.
- **SA-0MT2XRGEU0009QRE** — Audit in-main-slot mode (internal assertion): the mode that creates `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items.

# Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — fingerprint scoping is incomplete.** If child-relevant files/commits are not correctly identified, stale audits may still be invalidated or, conversely, genuinely stale audits may be reused. Mitigation: carefully identify the key files that each child audit covers; add a test case that simulates unrelated HEAD movement vs. child-relevant HEAD movement.
- **Risk — inheriting stale child verdicts masks real regressions.** If a child's code changed but the fingerprint didn't catch it, inheriting an old verdict is incorrect. Mitigation: the fingerprint scoping should cover all files relevant to the child audit.
- **Assumption:** all three suggested directions are desired (fingerprint scoping, partial-verdict handling, diagnostic clarity).
- **Assumption:** the audit runner is a Node.js/TypeScript or Python tool within the project; the fix applies to the runner's Python/TS source.

# Change the current mineral count to a bar that fills

## Problem statement

The ship's hold (minerals collected) is currently shown on the HUD as a text counter (`Minerals: n/20`). A text counter is visually weak in the neon-vector aesthetic and does not communicate "filling up" at a glance. Replace it with a fixed-length, hollow-outlined bar that fills proportionally as minerals are collected.

## Users

**Player** — needs to read hold progress instantly during fast play, without parsing digits.

- As a player, I want the hold shown as a bar that fills as I collect minerals, so that I can gauge progress toward the next power-up choice at a glance.
- As a player, I want the bar to show an empty hollow outline when I have no minerals, so that I can tell the hold exists and is empty.
- As a player, I want the bar to be the same length at all times, so that the layout does not shift and the relationship between fill and capacity stays readable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Bar replaces text.** When a mineral capacity is configured, the HUD renders a fixed-length horizontal bar row (outline + fill) in place of the `Minerals: n/20` text. The `Minerals:` text label is no longer the primary representation.
2. **Hollow when empty.** At `minerals = 0` only the hollow outline is visible (no fill pixels). The outline uses the existing neon HUD palette (cyan `#00ffff`).
3. **Proportional fill.** The filled portion grows linearly from the left: `0` at empty, full inner width at `minerals === capacity`; the fill width is clamped so it never exceeds or bleeds outside the outline. Any non-zero value renders a visible minimum fill so single-digit progress is perceptible.
4. **Stable row layout.** The bar row is hidden entirely when `capacity === 0` (gyms/game states without the mineral mechanic). The lives row and active effect/weapon rows keep their current positions with no overlap.
5. **Existing hold mechanics unchanged.** `GameState` arithmetic (`addMinerals`, `isHoldFull`, `resolveHold`, overflow) and the hold-full power-up choice are unaffected; the HUD only changes how the same values are rendered.
6. **Validated by unit tests.** A unit test asserts bar geometry at empty (`0/20`), mid (`10/20`) and full (`20/20`), the hollow-at-empty outline state, clamping at/over capacity, and row visibility for `capacity = 0`.
7. **Validation in-scene.** The `GymMinerals` gym and `PlayScene` show the bar filling as minerals are collected (manual/visual verification; `GymMinerals` test updated to assert the bar state instead of the removed text).
8. **Documentation updated.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and the Game Design Document §4.4.1 hold description (replace `Minerals: n/20` references with the bar). CHANGELOG.md is excluded (managed by the release pipeline).
9. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Must stay framework-idiomatic: the HUD is a `Phaser.GameObjects.Container`; the bar should be drawn with `Phaser.GameObjects.Graphics` (consistent with existing icon drawing), not DOM/CSS.
- Must not break the standalone-HUD contract: `src/ui/HUD.ts` has no gym-specific imports and binds to any scene.
- Must respect the neon aesthetic: "dark background with glowing neon outlines, minimal fill" (GDD §Visual Aesthetic).
- No new runtime dependency.

## Existing state

- `src/ui/HUD.ts` owns the mineral row via `_mineralLabel` (a `Text` object), `setMineralStore(minerals, capacity)`, `getMineralLabel()`, and `getMineralStoreValue()`. The row is shown when `_mineralCapacity > 0` and positioned below the lives row in `refresh()`.
- `src/core/GameState.ts` owns the authoritative hold (`minerals`, `mineralCapacity`, `addMinerals`, `isHoldFull`, `resolveHold`).
- Callers: `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (`_syncMineralHud`), `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts`.
- Tests referencing the text contract: `src/ui/__tests__/HUD.minerals.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.test.ts` (`getMineralLabel()` matching `/^Minerals: \d+\/20$/`).
- Docs referencing the text: `README.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.1.

## Desired change

`HUD` draws a fixed-size bar (predicted: ~120 px outline width × ~10 px height, exposed as named constants so it is tunable) at the existing mineral-row Y offset:

- Outer outline always drawn when `capacity > 0`, hollow at `minerals = 0`.
- Inner fill width = `round(innerWidth * clamp(minerals / capacity, 0, 1))`, with a small minimum fill for `minerals > 0`.
- Bar row hidden when `capacity = 0`.
- Public test accessor (e.g. `getMineralBarState(): { filled: number; total: number; visible: boolean }`) added; `getMineralStoreValue()` retained. `getMineralLabel()` is removed or repurposed as part of this change and its callers/tests updated.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — Replace `_mineralLabel` text row with a `Graphics`-drawn outline + fill bar; add bar geometry constants and `getMineralBarState()`; update row visibility/positioning.
- `src/ui/__tests__/HUD.minerals.test.ts` — Update to assert bar geometry (empty/mid/full), hollow outline, clamping, and hidden-when-capacity-0.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.test.ts` — Replace the `getMineralLabel()` text assertion with a bar-state assertion.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Confirm `_syncMineralHud` continues to drive the bar (likely no change beyond accessor usage).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — Confirm `setMineralStore` call-sites need no change.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Update §4.4.1 hold description (`Minerals: n/20` → filling bar).
- `README.md` — Update the HUD counter reference.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the bar *replaces* the numeric counter as the primary representation (per "change the current mineral count to a bar"); no numeric overlay is added. The underlying value remains exposed via `getMineralStoreValue()` and the new bar-state accessor.
- **Assumption:** bar dimensions/colours are implementation details to be tuned to the existing HUD row height (`HUD_ROW_HEIGHT = 22`).
- **Assumption:** the same HUD bar serves `PlayScene` and the gyms (the HUD already shares this row).
- **Risk (low):** HUD row-offset regression could overlap lives/effect rows — mitigated by AC4 tests and existing HUD tests.
- **Risk (low):** gym/PlayScene tests asserting the old text will fail until updated — captured in AC6/AC7 and the Key Files list.
- **Scope-creep risk:** adding numeric overlay, animation/easing of the fill, or colour changes at capacity are out of scope; record as separate work items if wanted.

## Related work

- Parent/related context: `Asteroids drop collectable minerals that fill the ship's hold and grant a power-up choice` (AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q) and its completed children (`AH-0MUCST45Q0054X19` HUD counter, `AH-0MUCST23S006AAMC` HUD counter tests).
- This change supersedes the text-counter rendering introduced by `AH-0MUCST45Q0054X19` (the hold store/overflow/HUD counter) while leaving its arithmetic intact.

### Related work (automated report)

#### Related work items

Add a new **Dev Utilities** category/section to the gym index, and create a gym scene within it that provides:

1. **Curve editor** — an interactive way to define the target difficulty curve (array of scores, one per wave)
2. **Regenerate button** — when clicked, runs the sequencer against the current curve and displays the resulting waves

# Wire the runtime auto-sequencer into the game's wave generation

## Problem statement

The runtime auto-sequencer (`src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`, AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X) is a standalone pure-core library — nothing in the playable game calls it. Enemy composition is still hard-coded in `src/waves/Formations.ts` (`LEVELS`) and driven through `WaveManager` by `PlayScene`, so every run uses the same fixed waves. This item wires the sequencer into a playable run so wave composition is generated at runtime from a target difficulty curve, behind an opt-in config toggle, with the static campaign preserved as the default and the fallback.

## Users

- As a **player**, when the feature is enabled, enemy waves should follow a difficulty curve so each run ramps up smoothly instead of using identical fixed enemy counts. (Default-off means shipped behaviour is unchanged until enabled.)
- As a **designer**, I want to define the campaign's levels, names, wave counts and per-wave difficulty targets in a CSV config, so I can tune the difficulty ramp and campaign shape without editing `Formations.ts`.

## Decisions confirmed at intake

1. **Opt-in toggle, default off.** Static `LEVELS` remains the shipped default; generated waves only drive the run when the toggle is enabled in config. A follow-on work item covers *mixing* generated and scripted levels within one campaign: **Support mixed generated and scripted levels in a campaign (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD)** (sibling, `discovered-from`).
2. **Per-level curves with configurable per-level wave counts.** One `sequencer()` call per level; the curve length sets the wave count.
3. **Fully data-driven campaign skeleton.** The curve config also defines the level count and level names (not just targets). The boss is still triggered after the final configured level (existing `WaveManager` behaviour).
4. **CSV-backed config.** A new `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` is loaded through the existing `configStore`/CSV pipeline (editable in dev via `/api/csv/...`, bundled read-only in production).
5. **Defaults seeded from current calibration.** The baked-in default targets are derived from the current `LEVELS` measured scores (`levelDifficulty`/`enemyDifficulty`) spread non-decreasingly across each level's waves.

## Existing state

- `WaveManager` already accepts injected `LevelDefinition[]` via its constructor and `setLevels()`, defaulting to static `LEVELS`; it owns plan/spawn/progression and the boss trigger.
- `sequencer(curve, candidates, options)` returns one `ShootableWave` per curve entry, each with one adjusted group and a `shootEnabled` flag; `options.defaultShootEnabled` applies to the whole call, which is why generation is done **per level** (so Levels 1–3 and 4–5 can differ).
- `AdjustedGroup` extends `WaveGroup`, so `ShootableWave.groups` maps structurally to `WaveDefinition.groups`.
- Config tunables live in two pipelines: CSV-backed `configStore`/`csv.ts`/Vite plugin (enemies, ship) and the localStorage-backed `rules.ts` (`GameRules`).
- GDD §2.4 — Levels 1–3 do not fire; §2.5 — Levels 4–5 do. §3.2 fixes level themes.

## Desired change

At run start, `PlayScene` reads the config. When the (opt-in) toggle is disabled it uses static `LEVELS` exactly as today. When enabled it builds a `LevelDefinition[]` from the difficulty-curve config by calling `sequencer()` once per configured level with `defaultShootEnabled = levelNumber >= 4`, converts each `ShootableWave` to a `WaveDefinition`, injects the result into `WaveManager`, and drives the run from it. Any empty/degenerate config falls back to static `LEVELS`.

## Constraints

- **Pure core stays pure.** `difficultySequencer.ts` is not modified (read-only call site).
- **Determinism.** Generation must be a pure function of config + candidate pool; no RNG.
- **No behavioural change when the toggle is off.** Existing `WaveManager`/`PlayScene`/campaign tests must pass unchanged.
- **CSV is the source of truth in dev**; production reads the bundled copy; malformed rows must not crash.
- Follow the existing config/CSV patterns (codec, plugin, store) rather than inventing a new persistence path.
- UK English in prose; Markdown in the work item.

## Assumptions

- The global opt-in toggle is a scalar tunable and will live in the existing `GameRules` settings store (`sequencedWavesEnabled`, default `false`); the per-level curve values/targets live in the CSV. Per-level source mixing is deferred to AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **WaveManager accepts injected definitions** — `WaveManager` is driven by generated `LevelDefinition`/`WaveDefinition` data; with no override supplied it uses static `LEVELS` exactly, and existing `WaveManager` tests pass unchanged.
2. **Opt-in toggle** — with the toggle disabled (the default) the run uses static `LEVELS` and behaves as today; with it enabled the run uses generated definitions (test asserts both paths).

6. **Curve is configurable** — changing the configured/default curve changes the produced wave composition; two distinct curves yield different plans (test asserts this).
7. **Campaign fire rule** — generated levels 1–3 have `shootEnabled=false`; levels 4+ have `shootEnabled=true` (test asserts both).
8. **Determinism** — generating the campaign twice with the same config and candidate pool yields identical level/wave definitions.
9. **Fallback is safe** — an empty/degenerate curve config, an empty curve, or an empty candidate pool falls back to static `LEVELS` and the game does not crash (test covers the fallback).
10. **Testing/validation** — new unit/integration tests cover the codec, campaign builder, conversion, fire rule, determinism and fallback, and they are meaningful and passing.
11. **Documentation** — all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
12. **No regressions** — the full project test suite passes with the new changes (`npm test`).

- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — **new** CSV defining levels, names, wave targets (data-driven skeleton).
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — **new**: build the curve config/pool and convert `SequencerResult` per level into `LevelDefinition[]` (plus fallback).
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — confirm/verify injected-definition support (minimal or no change).
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — static `LEVELS`: default/fallback and level metadata source for seeding defaults.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — build + inject the generated campaign at run start when the toggle is enabled.
- Vite CSV plugin / dev write endpoint — extend to serve the new CSV if the existing generic path does not already cover it.
- Test files: `src/core/csv.test.ts`, `src/core/configStore.test.ts`, `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts` (**new**), `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`.

- **Assumption (toggle location)** — the opt-in toggle lives in the `GameRules`/settings store rather than the CSV; revisit only if the producer prefers an all-CSV toggle.

# Goal

Fix the audit runner's parent-first flow so that child `partial` verdicts caused by unserviced in-main-slot items are treated as "not assessed" rather than blocking the parent's readiness-to-close decision, and add diagnostic clarity.

# Background

In `--child-in-main-slot` mode (default), child Phase-1 AC screens and Phase-2 deep analysis emit `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items for the invoking agent session. In non-interactive runs (e.g. downtime workers), these items are never serviced, leaving all child AC verdicts as `partial`.

Currently, `_build_issue_json` treats ALL `partial` verdicts as unacceptable, causing the parent to report "Ready to close: No" even when all parent ACs are met, because the child partials (from unserviced in-main-slot work) are counted as failures.

# Implementation Plan

## 1. Track in-main-slot partial verdicts

Add a `verdict_reason` field to child AC results when they are `partial` due to in-main-slot unserviced work. The `_phase1_review_child_acs` and `_deep_analyze_child` functions already set `verdict: "partial"` with evidence like `"pending (main-session review)"` in in-main-slot mode. We need to mark these explicitly with `verdict_reason: "unserviced-in-main-slot"`.

## 2. Handle partials in `_build_issue_json`

Modify `all_ac_acceptable` computation to skip child ACs whose `partial` verdict has `verdict_reason == "unserviced-in-main-slot"`. These should be treated as "not assessed" and NOT block the parent's readiness-to-close decision.

## 3. Add diagnostic output

In the audit summary/JSON output, surface a clear diagnostic that distinguishes:
- Children with `partial` verdicts from unserviced in-main-slot work → "not assessed"
- Children with genuine `partial` or `unmet` verdicts → "not-ready"

Add a `children_assessment` section to the `_build_issue_json` output listing `unserviced_in_main_slot` child IDs and `genuine_not_ready` child IDs.

# Acceptance Criteria
- AC2: Parent audit treats in-main-slot unserviced partials as "not assessed" (does NOT block ready-to-close)
- AC3: Audit output includes diagnostic distinguishing unserviced-in-main-slot partials from genuine failures

# Constraints
- Must not change behaviour of interactive runs (where agent CAN service in-main-slot items)
- Must be backward-compatible with persisted audit results

# Key Files
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_phase1_review_child_acs`, `_deep_analyze_child`, `_build_issue_json`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_child_in_main_slot.py` — existing in-main-slot tests
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` — freshness tests (verify no regression)

# Gym asteroids do not drop minerals — share the mineral kill-drop code with the game

## Headline

Gym asteroids do not drop minerals because the kill-drop rule lives only in the
game (`PlayScene`) while the gyms run a divergent copy. Extract the rule into one
shared helper used by both, and wire it into the gyms so they drop minerals
(small-asteroid single drop; non-asteroid 25–50 % re-drop) exactly as the game
does.

## Problem statement

Asteroids in the gym scenes do not drop minerals when destroyed, even though the
shipped game does and the gyms' own documentation says they should. The cause is
code divergence: the mineral **kill-drop** logic lives privately in `PlayScene`
and was never shared, while the gyms re-implemented the collection half of the
mineral layer and omitted the drop half. The fix is to make gym asteroids drop
minerals (per GDD §4.4.1) and to move the kill-drop logic into a single shared
helper used by both the game and the gyms, so the two can no longer drift.

## Users

- **As a player using the minerals gym**, when I destroy a small asteroid I want
  it to leave a mineral, so the gym demonstrates the real mechanic I see in the
  game.
- **As a player using the asteroid enemy gym**, when I destroy a small asteroid
  I want it to drop a mineral, so the gym matches the game's asteroid behaviour.
- **As a developer**, I want the mineral kill-drop logic to exist in exactly one
  shared place, so a gym and the game can never again disagree about whether an
  asteroid drops a mineral.
- **As a player**, when a non-asteroid enemy that has absorbed minerals is
  destroyed, I want it to re-drop a fraction of them, in the gym as in the game.

## Root cause (RCA summary)

- The shared base `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` provides the generic
  destruction seam (`onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy` → `onEnemyDestroyed`) but has no
  mineral concept.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` overrides `onEnemyDestroyed` and, in the private
  `_onEnemyKilled()`, implements the drops: small asteroid → `spawnMineralAt()`;
  large/medium asteroid → none (split children drop); non-asteroid enemy →
  `entity.spawnMineralDrops()` (25–50 % re-drop).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` re-implements the mineral layer
  (`seedMinerals`, `_initMineralLayer`, `_updateMinerals`) but its
  `onEntityDestroyed` path only splits asteroids — it never spawns a mineral and
  never calls `spawnMineralDrops()` on death.
- `GymMinerals.ts` (asteroids-only) and `GymEnemies.ts` (generic enemy gym, used
  for the "Asteroid" config row) both extend `GymFormationScene`, so both are
  affected.
- Prior unification work (AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO) shared the combat core but left
  the mineral logic duplicated — exactly the divergence the operator suspected.
- The gym docstrings and GDD §6.4 already claim "small-asteroid mineral drops …
  enemy absorption/re-drop"; the earlier gym item (AH-0MUCST5HA0079APB) had this
  in its acceptance criteria but it was closed without the drop behaviour.

## Existing state

- `BaseEnemy.mineralRedropCount()` / `spawnMineralDrops()` already implement the
  25–50 % re-drop and are unit-tested (AH-0MUCST3QD002O9TA / AH-0MUCST1P10004EXM).
- `PlayScene.spawnMineralAt()` is public and used by the game and, in principle,
  by gyms.
- `Asteroid.collectMineral()` is a no-op (asteroids are inert to minerals) and
  `Asteroid.getSizeTier()` / `getSplitChildren()` exist.
- `GymFormationScene` already owns a mineral field, a hold, a HUD counter and the
  hold-full choice overlay, and seeds 100 minerals on create.
- The rules config exposes `mineralCollectAmount`, `mineralHoldCapacity`,
  `mineralRedropFractionMin`/`Max`.

## Desired change

- Extract the mineral kill-drop rule into one shared helper used by **both**
  `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` (and therefore every formation gym).
  The helper decides, for a destroyed enemy, how many minerals to spawn and
  where: small asteroid → exactly one at the death site; large/medium asteroid →
  none; non-asteroid enemy → the configured fraction of minerals absorbed,
  scattered at the death site.
- Wire the helper into the gym destruction path so gym asteroids (and other
  gyms' enemies) drop minerals exactly as the game does.
- Leave gameplay values and balance unchanged; reuse the existing rules tunables.
- Keep the game's observable behaviour identical (pure refactor there), and keep
  the existing mineral tests green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Gyms drop on small-asteroid destruction.** Destroying a small asteroid
  in `GymMinerals` and in the `GymEnemies` asteroid-config row spawns exactly one
  mineral at the asteroid's position (matching `PlayScene`). Large/medium
  asteroids do not drop directly; their small split children do. Verified by a
  scene test that destroys a small asteroid and asserts the live mineral count
  increases by one at that position, and by a test that a large/medium asteroid
  splits without a direct drop.
- **AC2 — Gyms re-drop for non-asteroid enemies.** In a gym, a non-asteroid
  enemy that has absorbed minerals re-drops between the configured
  `mineralRedropFractionMin`/`Max` fraction of them (never more than collected)
  at its death site. Verified by a deterministic test injecting a seeded RNG.
- **AC3 — Single shared code path.** The mineral kill-drop rule (small-asteroid
  drop + non-asteroid re-drop) is implemented once in a shared helper/module and
  consumed by both `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene`; `PlayScene`'s private
  kill-drop block delegates to it. Verified by a parity/equivalence test and by
  the repo-wide duplicate-body guard passing.
- **AC4 — No game behaviour regression.** `PlayScene` mineral behaviour
  (small-asteroid drop, non-asteroid re-drop, collection, absorption, hold-fill
  choice) is unchanged; the existing `PlayScene` mineral tests stay green.
- **AC5 — Tests are added and green.** New/extended tests cover AC1–AC3 in the
  gym suites (`GymMinerals.test.ts`, `GymEnemies.test.ts`,
  `GymFormationScene.test.ts`) and all pass.
- **AC6 — Documentation updated.** The GDD (§4.4.1 and §6.4), the
  `GymMinerals`/`GymFormationScene` docstrings and any relevant README/docs
  entries describe the shared mineral kill-drop code and the gym behaviour.
- **AC7 — Full project test suite passes.** `npm test` (the full suite) passes
  with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Do not change balance/tuning values; use the existing rules config.
- Prefer a genuinely shared helper over per-scene copies (the operator selected
  the shared-helper approach); avoid introducing a second divergence.
- The extracted helper must not force gym-specific concerns (hold, HUD, choice)
  into the game, nor game-specific concerns (score, waves) into the gym.
- Tests must be meaningful and deterministic (TDD preferred); no snapshot-only
  or trivially-true assertions.
- Written output and docs in UK English.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — likely host for, or hook to, the shared
  mineral kill-drop helper (shared base of game and gyms).
- `src/scenes/core/<new mineral helper>.ts` (or `src/core/minerals.ts`) — the
  single shared implementation of the kill-drop rule.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — refactor `_onEnemyKilled()` mineral block to
  delegate to the shared helper (no behaviour change).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — call the shared helper from the
  destruction path; add dropped minerals to the gym's mineral field.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — reuse `spawnMineralDrops()` / `mineralRedropCount()`.
- `src/entities/Asteroid.ts` — reuse `getSizeTier()` / `getSplitChildren()`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.minerals.test.ts` — tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4.1 / §6.4 wording and gym docstrings.

## Related work

- `AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q` — parent mechanic (asteroids drop minerals; hold; choice).
- `AH-0MUCST5HA0079APB` — asteroids-only mineral gym; its AC claimed small-asteroid
  drops and enemy re-drop, but the drop half was not implemented (this item closes
  that gap).
- `AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO` — prior unification of PlayScene/GymFormationScene combat
  logic into a shared core; this item extends the same principle to minerals.
- `AH-0MUCST3QD002O9TA` — mineral rules tunables and per-enemy mineral count.
- `AH-0MUCST1P10004EXM` — tests for enemy mineral count and re-drop distribution.
- `AH-0MUCST3BS0007CPT` — Mineral collectable entity and constants.
- `AH-0MUHMXWGC0058BO4` — ability items (Dual Shot/Teleport/Phase Shift) not
  functioning; a distinct gym-sharing defect, not a mineral drop issue.
- `AH-0MUHM66ES0027QQV` — enemy gym P3/P6 hit-gating not shared; a distinct
  gym-sharing defect, not a mineral drop issue.

## Out of scope

- Fixing the distinct gym-sharing defects `AH-0MUHMXWGC0058BO4` (ability items)
  and `AH-0MUHM66ES0027QQV` (enemy gym P3/P6 hit-gating).
- Any change to mineral balance/tuning values or the hold/choice reward pool.

## Goal
Fix the displayed-vs-applied option divergence in the main-game mineral choice overlay so the player sees and gets the same option.

## Root Cause
`PlayScene.openMineralChoice()` draws options via `this.mineralChoiceStrategy.choose(3, this.rng)` and stores them in `this.mineralChoiceOptions`, but only passes `{ origin: 'PlayScene' }` to the MineralChoiceScene overlay. `MineralChoiceScene.init()` then draws its own independent options via `randomChoiceStrategy.choose(3)` when `options` is absent. `selectMineralChoice(index)` applies `play.mineralChoiceOptions[index]` — a different draw from the label shown.

## Goal
Make P7 Teleport operational in the minerals gym by wiring key binding, handler invocation, and canTeleport override.

## Root Cause
GymMinerals' asteroidFormationConfig() omits the `powerUps` config key, so GymFormationScene.powerUpsEnabled stays false. Consequently:
- _initPowerUpLayer() returns early and never binds the S/keys
- _updatePowerUpLayer() returns early and never calls _handleTeleport()
- canTeleport() returns powerUpsEnabled (false)

## Implementation
1. In GymFormationScene, bind the teleport key (S/Down) whenever a player exists, independent of powerUpsEnabled.
2. In GymFormationScene, call _handleTeleport() each tick whenever hasTeleport() is true, independent of powerUpsEnabled.
3. Override canTeleport() to return hasTeleport() in addition to powerUpsEnabled.
4. Ensure _handleTeleport() triggers P6 Phase Shift on arrival (as per GDD and AH-0MT7UY5UR002LD5U).

## Risks
- S is also the "down" movement key; use JustDown semantics to avoid double-consumption.
- Must not affect other gyms that rely on powerUpsEnabled gating.

- **AC2 — P7 Teleport works in the minerals gym:** after a P7 Teleport is granted, stack decremented, player position changed, isPhased true.

## Goal
Wire the shared EffectsRegistry into GymFormationScene's combat hooks so P6 (Phase Shift) and P3 (Shield) granted via the mineral reward choice are honoured.

## Root Cause
GymFormationScene does not override isPlayerPhased() or tryAbsorbPlayerHit(), so CombatCoreScene's defaults (false) are used even though EffectsRegistry.isPhased / isShielded are true. The mineral reward can grant these effects, but _handleCollisions() never honours them.

1. Override isPlayerPhased() in GymFormationScene to return registry.isPhased.
2. Override tryAbsorbPlayerHit() in GymFormationScene to:
   - Return true (absorb) when registry.isShielded is true and pop the shield.
   - Delegate to the parent/hook chain for other logic.
3. Follow the pattern from GymPowerUpsCombat.ts which already overrides these hooks correctly.

- **AC3 — P6 Phase Shift protects in the minerals gym:** while P6 is active, enemy bullets and bodies do not register a hit; playerHitCount unchanged.

# Test: shared mineral kill-drop rule

Test-first task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC3, AC5).

## Goal

Write deterministic unit + guard tests that pin the contract of the shared mineral kill-drop rule **before** it is implemented, so `PlayScene` and the gyms provably share one rule.

## Required coverage

- Small asteroid (`getSizeTier() === 'small'`) → exactly one mineral drop at the asteroid's death position.
- Large and medium asteroid → no direct drop (their small split children drop).
- Non-asteroid enemy that absorbed N minerals → re-drops between `mineralRedropFractionMin` and `mineralRedropFractionMax` of N, never more than N, at the death site, using a seeded RNG for determinism.
- Non-asteroid enemy with 0 absorbed minerals → no drops.
- Re-drop scatter stays within `MINERAL_REDROP_SCATTER_RADIUS` of the death site.
- Guard/parity: the shared kill-drop rule is defined exactly once repo-wide, and both `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` reference it (extend `src/test/duplicateBodyGuard.ts` / `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` as needed).

## Assumption

Shared helper module path: `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` exporting `resolveMineralKillDrops(scene, entity, rng): Mineral[]` (operator selected the shared-helper approach — see the parent item's Appendix).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Unit tests exist for the shared kill-drop rule covering each bullet above and are deterministic (seeded RNG, no reliance on `Math.random`).
- A repo-wide guard asserts the kill-drop rule has a single production definition and that both scenes consume it.
- Tests fail before the implementation task lands and pass once it does.
- `npm test` for the new/extended test files passes after implementation.
